newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak bourse to realign trading into three mkts.
newsitem.headline: Slovak bourse to realign trading into three mkts.

text.p: Slovakia's Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Friday it would realign shares on the bourse into three markets beginning in August from its current two, in order to better identify shares by liquidity.

The new division will include the main listed stock market, a registered shares market and a free market trading all remaining issues which will not qualify for the first two markets, the BSE said in a statement.
At present, shares are traded on two BSE markets called the listed and unlisted floors.
"The new listed floor will contain the best issues which will have to meet all the current criteria for listing," Barbora Lazarova, head of the BSE Listing Division, told Reuters.
The new BSE listed floor will start trading 13 leading stocks when the division becomes effective on August 1. The BSE said the listed market can grow to as many as 50 issues.
Companies traded on the new listed floor must have a minimum basic capital of 500 million crowns ($14.4 million) and will be required to report quarterly results to the BSE, Lazarova said.
Firms traded on the registered floor must have a basic capital of 100 million crowns and will have to present half-year results
The registered floor will contain 44 issues from August and is expected to expand to some 100 items.
Lazarova said the main criteria distinguishing shares on the registered floor and on the free market will be their liquidity.

"But no exact liquidity volume will be set. We will assess shares trading over a certain period and we can move issues from the registered to the free market if their liquidity radically changes," she added
No special admission criteria, except those stipulated by law for issuing shares, will have to be fulfiled for introducing shares to the free market.
The BSE is one the smallest bourses in post-Communist Europe with market capitalisation of $2.6 billion, compared with the region's largest, Prague, which has a capitalisation of some $16 billion.
-- Peter Laca, Bratislava Newsroom, 421-7-521-8402 ($ = 34.67 Slovak Crowns)
